annotations.title: A passage with its surrounding verses

description: Read a verse or short range together with the verses immediately before and after it (default 3 each side, up to 10), verbatim from the stored King James Version, crossing into the neighbouring chapter of the same book when needed. Use when a verse needs its context ("Jeremiah 29:11 in context", "what comes before John 3:16"). For the passage alone or a whole chapter use scripture_passage (a chapter reference here returns an error pointing to it); for related passages elsewhere in the Bible use cross_references. around applies to each side; a range keeps all its verses. Deterministic; the evidence field carries translation and content hashes. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

around.description: Verses to read on each side, 0 to 10 (default 3).

reference.description: One verse or a short range, not a whole chapter: "Jeremiah 29:11", "Romans 8:28-30".

name: scripture_context

after.description: The verses just after, or null at the end of the book.

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

before.description: The verses just before, or null at the start of the book.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

passage.description: The passage itself: ref, verbatim text, and verses.

ref.description: Normalised reference of the passage asked for.

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.
